description: By design of the fix, an orphan temp file (<id>.run-state.json.<uuid>.tmp) that a save cannot remove (persistent EACCES, EISDIR, EROFS...) makes EVERY save of that run id fail with io-error (EPERM/EBUSY that outlast 1.5 s: conflict) until an operator removes the file; the message names the file. A dead writer's undeletable temp therefore blocks that one run id instead of letting a possibly-live displaced writer's rename land. Also: the reap now runs on every lock acquisition (one directory listing per save), not only after a takeover; the old pinned test 'a live writer's temp is never touched when the lock was free' was rewritten because a temp under a freshly acquired lock can only be a previous holder's. Low: documented trade-off, not a defect; ledger only.
repro: run-state-reap-refusal.test.ts 'dead holder, orphan temp that stays undeletable (EACCES)'.
fix_direction: None needed. If operators need it, a wiring-time admin path that lists/removes orphan temps.
